subject.title: Feature: Telegram Reactions - Two-Way Support with Prompt Guidance

question: Should Telegram reaction prompt guidance be controlled by a new `reactionGuidance` config option, or should incoming/outbound guidance stay folded into existing `reactionLevel` and `reactionNotifications` semantics?
rationale: The request adds a public prompt-affecting config/default surface, and OpenClaw policy sets a high bar for new config knobs that overlap existing channel behavior.

options.title: Use existing reaction config
options.body: Keep `reactionLevel` as the outbound guidance control and gate incoming soft-CTA guidance on `reactionNotifications`, avoiding a third reaction config knob.

options.title: Add reactionGuidance explicitly
options.body: Add `reactionGuidance: off|minimal|full` with config schema, metadata, docs, and tests that define how it composes with `reactionLevel` and `reactionNotifications`.

options.title: Decline prompt semantics
options.body: Keep reactions as raw events and message-tool actions only, leaving semantic interpretation to user prompts or future plugin policy.

recommendation.title: Use existing reaction config
recommendation.body: Keep `reactionLevel` as the outbound guidance control and gate incoming soft-CTA guidance on `reactionNotifications`, avoiding a third reaction config knob.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this issue and has the strongest recent history on Telegram reaction defaults and config semantics.
